text: Photography begins with the shutter, the mechanism that opens to admit light into the device. A rapid shutter speed records only a brief segment of available illumination yet succeeds in stopping motion effectively. Subsequently, aperture controls the volume of light reaching the sensor. This opening widens during low-light conditions and narrows when brightness is high. Selecting a small aperture results in higher total light intake paired with slower shutter speeds, whereas a wide aperture admits greater amounts of light while permitting faster shutter operations.
